title: Phantom Blade Zero Endings - What Is Known Before Launch
description: Phantom Blade Zero endings explained as far as they can be before release: the confirmed story premise, why a branching conclusion is expected, and what remains unverified until October 29, 2026.

sections.title: Short Answer: The Endings Are Not Officially Detailed Yet
sections.content:
Phantom Blade Zero has not been released. S-GAME has not published an official ending count, ending names, or the conditions that trigger them. Anything you read elsewhere with a specific number of endings is either a guess or taken from an unofficial source.

This page covers what is confirmed about how the story concludes, and marks clearly where verified information stops. It will be expanded once the game is out and the endings can actually be played.

sections.title: The Premise That Frames the Ending
sections.content:
What is confirmed is the setup, and it is unusually tight — which is why an ending that resolves it matters so much.

You play as Soul, an elite assassin serving a powerful and elusive organisation known simply as The Order. Soul is framed for the murder of The Order's patriarch and gravely injured during the manhunt that follows. A figure credited as The Flesh Sculptor revives him with a tainted heart, and the makeshift cure lasts only 66 days.

The game's driving objective is therefore explicit: find the mastermind behind the framing before the 66 days run out. That is a premise built to end a specific way — with the countdown reaching zero.

sections.title: Why Multiple Endings Are Expected
sections.content:
There is no official confirmation of branching endings. However, several confirmed design facts make a choice-driven conclusion likely:

  • The 66-day countdown creates a natural deadline that a story can resolve in more than one way
  • The game is structured as an action RPG with a semi-open world and optional content, which is the structure that usually supports divergent outcomes
  • S-GAME has described the story in terms of themes — revenge, hatred and love — rather than a single fixed arc

That is reasoning, not confirmation. Treat it as expectation, not fact, until the game ships.

sections.title: Claims You Should Not Trust Yet
sections.content:
Because the game has not released, a number of sites publish content that cannot be true. The most common patterns to watch for:

Claim typeWhy it is unverifiable
"All 8 endings" or any specific countNo official figure exists; endings cannot be enumerated before release
"Unlock requirements" per endingRequires a shipped build that players can complete
Hands-on impressions and hours playedThe finished game is not available to play
Full boss lists and stat tablesFinal content is only knowable post-launch

Some of these pages are written confidently and rank well. Confidence is not evidence — the game's own store pages and S-GAME's announcements are the only sources that count before launch.

sections.title: What Happens After October 29
sections.content:
Once the game launches, this page will be rebuilt with actual information: the real ending count, the decisions that produce each outcome, and how they relate to the 66-day structure.

In the meantime, the confirmed background is worth reading:

  • Release date and platform details
  • Soul and the story premise
  • The studio behind the game
  • The Sha-chi combat system

sections.title: 饮恨江湖 - The 66 Days Failure Ending
sections.content:
Community documentation names an ending that the official material has not: 饮恨江湖, reached when the day counter in 66 Days mode hits zero. The BWIKI wording is explicit - 天数归零则进入"饮恨江湖"结局 - and it matters more than a game-over screen, because it means the permadeath failure state is authored into the ending list rather than sitting outside it.

Put against the reported total of eight endings, a failure state with its own name implies it is being counted, which in turn implies the counter is part of the ending map rather than a bonus mode bolted onto it. That is inference from two sources, not a statement from either.

Status: community-sourced, unconfirmed by S-GAME. No English name has been published. The literal sense is something like "harbouring resentment in the jianghu" - dying with the grudge unspent.

Source: 影之刃 WIKI on BWIKI (难度与成就, revision 2896, edited 2026-10-11), a fan wiki run by 影之刃 Tieba moderators, unaffiliated with S-GAME.
